checks.claim: Nitrifying one gram of ammonia nitrogen into nitrate uses about 4.57 grams of oxygen.
checks.why: A Water Research paper and a wastewater patent both give 4.57 g O2 per g ammonia-N as the theoretical stoichiometry for complete oxidation to nitrate. It is a theoretical figure, and real systems differ slightly.

sources.title: Probing the stoichiometry of the nitrification process using the respirometric approach - ScienceDirect
Method for treating nitrogen in waste streams

checks.claim: Long-term exposure to unionized ammonia above about 0.02 mg per liter is generally considered potentially harmful to fish, including their gills; some guides put the damage point nearer 0.05 mg per liter.
checks.why: 0.02 mg/L is a general or chronic safety threshold, not a specific gill-damage onset. Sources differ, and Texas A&M uses 0.05 mg/L. One tilapia study links continuous exposure above 0.02 mg/L to gill irritation.

sources.title: Evaluation of acute toxicity of ammonia in Genetically Improved Farmed Tilapia - ScienceDirect

checks.claim: Fresh water holds about 14.6 mg of oxygen per liter at 0 degrees C but only about 7.6 mg per liter at 30 degrees C (at saturation and sea-level pressure).
checks.why: Tables give 14.60-14.62 mg/L at 0 C and 7.54-7.56 mg/L at 30 C, so about 7.6 is acceptable. This holds for saturated fresh water at sea-level pressure.
